grades.quote: In a race, two threads use the same data structure, without any mechanism to ensure only one thread uses the data structure at a time. If either thread precedes the other, all is well. However, if the two are interleaved, the program malfunctions.
grades.reason: Explains the race condition behind lost updates. Two threads interleave on shared data with no mutual exclusion, and the passage notes that two threads can each dispense a ticket yet leave seatsRemaining at 1 instead of 0. The example is a check-then-decrement on seat counts, not an increment of a counter. It also doesn't break down the read-modify-write steps, so it is useful but indirect.
Covers scheduling policy and denial-of-service resistance. It says nothing about shared-counter races or lost updates.
Covers fair-share and proportional-share scheduling. It is unrelated to concurrent increments on a shared counter.
